predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: T=(1.3,0.55,0), R=Rz(50deg), S=diag(1,2.4,1). Composed left-to-right by pre-multiplication over the figure's 11 vertices; mean vertex distance across all 15 pairs. RST(T*S*R) vs SRT(T*R*S) minimum at 0.489 m; 0.489/4.4 span = 11.1% of width, figure ~1/4 of frame -> ~2.8%. Sanity check in the same run: TSR vs STR came out 0.770 m, matching the closed form S*t - t = (0, 0.55*1.4, 0) exactly.

order_matters.name: Order Matters
order_matters.description: Transformation's cheat-code as an object rather than a diagram: ONE figure, ONE translation (1.3, 0.55, 0), ONE rotation (50 degrees about Z), ONE NON-UNIFORM scale (1, 2.4, 1) - and the six orders you can apply them in. Letters read left to right as world-space application, so TRS builds S*R*T. The scale is non-uniform on purpose: a uniform scale commutes with rotation and the axis would die quietly. A pale ghost of the untouched figure stands at the origin in every frame. The numbers never change; six different objects come out. 2026-08-27.
